name: TPS22810DRVR
title: TPS22810: 2.7 V to 18 V, 79 mΩ single-channel load switch with thermal shutdown
summary: A one-channel load switch built round an internal N-channel MOSFET, running from 2.7 V to 18 V with 79 mΩ typical on-resistance. A capacitor on CT sets the output ramp to hold down inrush; QOD gives an output discharge whose rate is set by an external resistor, by the internal pull-down alone, or is turned off. EN/UVLO is an active-high enable with a 1.23 V rising threshold that doubles as an adjustable undervoltage lockout; an internal VIN lockout and thermal shutdown complete the protection. The SOT-23 (DBV) part carries 2 A and the 2 mm × 2 mm WSON (DRV) part 3 A continuous at 65 °C ambient.
key_figures: 2.7 V to 18 V (20 V absolute maximum)

circuits.title: Typical application
circuits.description: The switch sits between a supply and a downstream load. CIN decouples VIN; the load is CL in parallel with RL. REXT from VOUT to QOD adds to the internal pull-down to set the discharge rate, and the capacitor on CT stretches the turn-on ramp to limit inrush into CL. An ON/OFF control signal drives EN/UVLO. The values are those of the worked design: 12 V in, 2 A load, 22 µF load capacitance, 20 ms fall time and under 400 mA of inrush.

parts.note: with RPD ≈ 250 Ω at 12 V gives RQOD = 413.7 Ω
957 µs typical rise at 12 V, about 220 mA inrush

circuits.title: Undervoltage lockout set by an external divider
circuits.description: R1 from VIN and R2 to ground form a divider into EN/UVLO, so the switch turns on when the divided input crosses the 1.23 V rising threshold and off below 1.13 V. CIN decouples the input and CL loads the output. CT and QOD are left open: default ramp, no output discharge.

circuits.title: Enable driven straight from a 1.8 V or 3.3 V GPIO
circuits.description: A processor GPIO drives EN/UVLO directly; the low enable threshold suits 1.8 V and 3.3 V logic. The internal VIN lockout at 2.54 V rising still applies. CIN decouples the input, CL loads the output, CT and QOD are open.

circuits.title: Default VIN lockout, EN/UVLO tied to VIN
circuits.description: EN/UVLO is joined to VIN, so the switch is on whenever the input is above the internal lockout (2.54 V typical rising, 5 % hysteresis) and needs no parts beyond CIN and CL. CT and QOD are open.

circuits.title: Switching-time test circuit
circuits.description: The circuit the switching times are measured in. A voltage source with a 1 µF capacitor feeds VIN, a step generator with 100 ns edges drives EN/UVLO, and the output is loaded with CL in parallel with RL (0.1 µF and 10 Ω in the switching table). CT and QOD are not connected.

parts.value: ON/OFF step, 100 ns rise and fall

notes: The switching characteristics are specified with RL = 10 Ω, CL = 0.1 µF and CT = 2200 pF.

operation.text: An N-channel MOSFET with its own charge pump, control logic, driver and discharge FET, so no external parts are needed to switch. Once VIN is above the rising lockout VUVR, the part looks at EN/UVLO; a high level turns the MOSFET on and current flows from VIN to VOUT. Off, its leakage is low, which keeps standby current in downstream circuits small.

A high on EN/UVLO turns the switch on. Below VENF (1.13 V typical) the MOSFET is off and VIN is disconnected from VOUT; below VSHUTF (0.75 V typical) the whole part shuts down and draws under 1 µA. The thresholds suit any GPIO of 1.2 V or more, and 1.8 V, 3.3 V and 5 V outputs can drive the pin directly. The pin must not float.

The falling-edge deglitch on EN/UVLO is short, 2.5 µs typical, so a power failure is caught fast. Adding capacitance between EN/UVLO and ground lengthens it, for a noisy supply or where a slower response is wanted.

A divider from VIN to EN/UVLO to GND sets an input lockout level against the 1.23 V / 1.13 V enable thresholds; on a detected undervoltage or input failure the MOSFET turns off quickly. Without the divider, EN/UVLO is tied to VIN. Separately, an internal lockout on VIN turns the part off when VIN falls below its falling threshold; its hysteresis is 125 mV, 5 % of VUVR (2.54 V rising, 2.4 V falling).

QOD has three settings. Tied to VOUT, the output is discharged through the internal RPD when the switch turns off. Through an external REXT to VOUT, the discharge resistance is RPD + REXT, which also makes the fall time depend less on VIN. Left open, there is no discharge and the output floats once off. The discharge is not active during thermal shutdown.

operation.topic: Discharge when the supply is removed
operation.text: QOD can sequence rails down even when the system supply disappears: CIN discharges and, once VIN passes the lockout, RPD is disconnected and any charge left on the output decays slowly. CIN has to be large enough to hold VIN above the lockout for the discharge to finish. Several switches with chosen CL and RQOD values give a set order of rails falling.

Using the internal RPD alone, the load capacitance must not exceed 200 µF, to keep the junction below 125 °C during discharge; above that, add REXT to limit the current through RPD. The output must be left to decay through the discharge path, not driven.

A capacitor from CT to GND sets the output slew rate; the CT pin rises to as much as 2.5 V. The slow ramp cuts inrush into large load capacitance and the droop it causes on the supply. Rise times hold for turn-on with VIN already steady before EN/UVLO goes high.

The switch turns off when the junction passes TSD (160 °C typical) and turns back on once it has cooled by the hysteresis (30 °C typical). This also covers over-current heating, so the safe operating area needs no separate design work.

Turning on into an empty load capacitor pulls current that sags the supply; capacitance from VIN to GND holds it up. 1 µF of ceramic next to the part normally does; more helps at high current, and for heavy loads about ten times CL is the guide.

The MOSFET's body diode conducts from VOUT to VIN if VOUT rises above VIN, which a CL larger than CIN can cause when the supply is removed; CIN should exceed CL. A CIN:CL ratio of 10:1 minimises the input dip at turn-on but is not required; a smaller ratio such as 1:1 gives a somewhat larger dip, which a larger CT reduces.

The supply should be well regulated, with a 1 µF ceramic bypass at the device. A supply several inches or more away may need added bulk capacitance (electrolytic, tantalum or ceramic; 1 µF may be enough). VIN and EN/UVLO may be applied in either order, within the absolute maximum ratings.

Keep the VIN and VOUT traces short and wide for the current. Decouple VIN with X5R or X7R ceramic of low ESR, 1 µF typical, as close to the pins as possible. Place input and output capacitors close to the part to keep trace inductance low; wide VIN, VOUT and GND copper also lowers case-to-ambient thermal resistance. The example layout takes GND to the power ground plane through vias at the pin.
The junction is to stay at or below 150 °C in normal operation; the allowable dissipation follows from θJA, which depends strongly on the board.

Times are referred to the 50 % point of the control step. tD runs to VOUT reaching 10 %; tON runs to VOUT reaching 50 % (also written tOUT); tOFF runs from the falling control edge to VOUT at 50 %. tR is VOUT from 10 % to 90 %; tF is VOUT falling from 90 % to 10 %; the timing diagram labels the fall end point 100 %, which should read 10 %.
